title: Grappler Baki: Natty or Not?
summary: NH goes through the Grappler Baki cast and judges whether each physique could be built naturally, based on looks rather than the often inconsistent stated stats. Most leads are unrealistic, but Kato, Kosho, Motobe, Captain Strydum, Endo, manga Gaia and Toba are presented as achievable natural goals.
claims: Using fictional physiques as goals helps set realistic expectations if you sort what is natty-achievable
Baki at 13, 5'2" and 160 lb lean is implausible for a prepubescent boy, but the same body is achievable for most adults
Gaining 20 lb without adding body fat is unrealistic; never gain that much weight that fast even if skinny
Very lean and very big at the same time is the clearest marker of an unnatural physique
Motobe at 51 is the most realistic physique in the show; staying in shape gets you a similar body at that age
Jack Hanma's 255 lb at 6'3" is reachable for a tall lifter after about a decade of training, but his look isn't
Retsu's 233 lb at 5'9" and his lats are not natural
Kato and Kosho, around 180 lb, have true martial-artist bodies and are accessible standards for bodybuilders
Huge traps and tree-trunk legs are rarely seen in real professional fighters
Captain Strydum looks like an ex-military man doing bodybuilding on the side and gets a natty card
Hanayama's 366 lb with a six-pack isn't achievable even with drugs
Endo, a 6'6" strength-focused man carrying body fat, is a natural goal for anyone willing to gain fat
Yujiro's 265 lb at 6'2" is doable, but not at around 5% body fat year-round
Manga Gaia (5'3", 130 lb) is easy: focus on abs and arms plus push-ups and sit-ups
Very tall men need far more mass to look muscular; Toba at 6'10" and 330 lb is realistic despite thin arms
Aiming at an impossible body is fine if you accept you may land short
